q.q: What is programming often called?
q.why: Programming is often called coding because it involves writing in a language computers understand.

q.q: Besides writing code, what else does a programmer do?
o: Builds the hardware the code will run on
Tests the code to make sure it works properly
Converts the code into binary by hand
q.why: A programmer writes code and tests it to make sure it is fully functional.

q.q: Who wrote what is seen as the first algorithm intended to be carried out by a machine?
q.why: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm intended for a machine; Babbage designed the Analytical Engine.

q.q: In 1843, what did Ada Lovelace's algorithm calculate?
q.why: Her algorithm calculated a series called the Bernoulli numbers.

q.q: Roughly how many programming languages are in use today?
q.why: There are about 700, because different jobs need different features.

q.q: A program decides whether to run a group of lines using an IF statement. Which basic concept is this?
q.why: Selection decides whether a line or group of lines should be run.

q.q: 'Working with ideas rather than physical things' describes which thinking skill?
q.why: Abstract means working with concepts rather than physical things.

q.q: 'Pulling information out of a scenario to understand the problem' describes which skill?
q.why: Analysis means understanding the problem so you can create sensible solutions.

q.q: Who wrote the C# language?
q.why: C# was written by Microsoft; NASA and Unity use it.

q.q: C# applications run on which framework?
q.why: C# runs on Microsoft's .NET framework.

q.q: Which of these languages is close to human-readable English?
q.why: High-level languages are close to human-readable English.

q.q: What does a compiler do?
o: Shows the program's output in a text-only window on screen
Predicts the next word of code as you type, like predictive text
Underlines syntax errors in red as you are typing the code
Converts human-readable code into binary the computer understands
q.why: Compiling turns source code into binary; red underlines and predictive text are IDE features.

q.q: What does it mean that C# is strongly typed?
o: Variables can change from text to numbers at any time
You must say what type of data each variable holds before using it
Code must be typed in capital letters only
You must type every line of code without using copy and paste
q.why: Strong typing means stating the data type of each variable.

q.q: What is IntelliSense?
o: A tool that converts code to binary
q.why: IntelliSense is one benefit of strong typing: it predicts code as you type.

q.q: What is an IDE?
o: Software that brings tools for writing, testing and running code together
A list of all the data types that can be used in a C# program
A text-only window where the output of a console program appears
A program that turns machine code back into C# so you can read it
q.why: An Integrated Development Environment such as Visual Studio has all the tools in one place.

q.q: Visual Studio puts a red underline under part of your code. What does it mean?
q.why: Red underlines mark errors; comments are shown in green.

q.q: Which project template should you choose in Visual Studio for these lessons?
q.why: Pick the Console App template and make sure it is the C# version.

q.q: When a C# console program is run, which part runs first?
q.why: Every program starts in the Main method, the first 'chapter'.

q.q: In the book series comparison, what does the class represent?
q.why: The namespace is the series, the class is a book, Main is a chapter and statements are sentences.

q.q: Which line correctly displays Hello?
q.why: It has the right capitals, speech marks, brackets and semicolon.

q.q: Which character is C#'s 'full stop' at the end of every statement?
q.why: The semicolon is the line terminator, C#'s full stop.

q.q: In Console.WriteLine("Hi"); what is WriteLine?
q.why: Console is the object, WriteLine is the method and "Hi" is the message.

q.q: The Error List shows 'error CS1002: ; expected'. What is wrong?
o: A semicolon is missing at the end of a line
A comment has been typed in the wrong place
A variable has the wrong data type
The Main method has been spelt wrongly
q.why: CS1002 means a semicolon is expected.

q.q: Which line is a comment?
q.why: Anything after // is ignored by the computer.

q.q: Why might a programmer put // in front of a working line of code?
o: To turn the line's text green on the screen
To make the line run twice as fast
To switch off the line and see how the program runs without it
To make the line run before every other line
q.why: Comments are ignored, so commenting a line out switches it off.

q.q: What is syntax?
o: The set of rules defining how code must be written
The text window where output appears
The software where we write code
The character used to end a statement
q.why: Syntax is the rules of the language; the console is the window.

q.q: What is a variable?
o: A named storage box in memory whose value can change
A rule about how code must be written
A method that displays text on the screen
A value that can never change once the program runs
q.why: A variable holds data in RAM and its value can change.

q.q: What two things must you define before you can put anything into a variable?
o: Its data type and its name
Its data type and its comment
Its name and its line number
q.why: In C# you state the data type and name first.

q.q: Which C# data type is the right choice for a price such as 4.50?
q.why: It has a decimal point, so it needs a double.

q.q: Which data type should store a scoreboard value such as 19?
q.why: Whole numbers are stored as int.

q.q: Which C# data type would you use for isMember, which can only be true or false?
q.why: bool holds Boolean values.

q.q: Which value is a correct char?
q.why: A char is a single character in single quotes; double quotes are for strings.

q.q: Which is a correct declaration?
q.why: Type, name, =, value, semicolon.

q.q: Which variable name follows the rules and uses camelCase?
q.why: No spaces or symbols, starts with a letter and each new word has a capital.

q.q: Why can't 'class' be used as a variable name?
o: It does not start with a capital letter
It is too short to be descriptive
It is a reserved keyword in C#
q.why: Words C# already uses, like int, class and lock, are reserved.

q.q: What is the = sign called in int score = 50;?
q.why: = stores the value on the right in the variable on the left.

q.q: Specifying the name and data type for a new variable is known as...
q.why: Creating the variable is called declaration.

q.q: What is joining strings together with + called?
q.why: Concatenation joins text and variables.

q.q: If profession holds "Coding Wizard", what does Console.WriteLine("Hello" + profession); output?
q.why: With no space inside the speech marks the words are squashed together.

q.q: What does string a = "3"; string b = "4"; Console.WriteLine(a + b); print?
q.why: Strings are joined, not added.

q.q: What does Console.WriteLine("Total: " + 4 + 5); print?
q.why: The text comes first, so + joins 4 and 5 as text.

q.q: age holds 15. What does Console.WriteLine("I will be " + (age + 10)); print?
q.why: The brackets make the addition happen first: 15 + 10 = 25.

q.q: With no brackets around the sum, what does Console.WriteLine("I will be " + age + 10); print when age holds 15?
q.why: Without brackets, "15" and "10" are joined as text.

q.q: Which line has an error?
q.why: A variable name cannot contain a full stop.

q.q: What is wrong with the line int number = 38498.3222; ?
o: The number is too big for an int
The name number is a reserved keyword
An int must be a whole number
q.why: 38498.3222 has a decimal part, so it needs a double.

q.q: What is wrong with the line dinosaur = "Barney"; if dinosaur has not been used before?
o: It has not been declared with a data type
dinosaur should start with a capital
Barney should be in single quotes
q.why: A variable must be declared with a type: string dinosaur = "Barney";

q.q: What is the real problem with double lock = 293.000; ?
o: 293.000 must be stored in an int instead of a double
The value 293.000 needs to be written in double quotes
lock is a reserved keyword, so it can't be a variable name
A double can only ever have two decimal places in C#
q.why: 293.000 is a perfectly good double; the problem is the name lock.

q.q: Why does C# make us use int and double instead of storing everything as a string?
o: Strings cannot be displayed on the screen
int and double are faster to type
Text is joined with +, so maths would not work properly
Strings take up no memory at all

q.q: What does Console.ReadLine() do?
o: Displays a line of text on the screen for the user
Pauses the program until the user types and presses Enter
Reads the next line of the program's own code
Converts the text that was typed into a whole number
q.why: ReadLine waits for input; WriteLine displays text.

q.q: What data type does Console.ReadLine() always return?
q.why: It always returns a string, even if the user types a number.

q.q: Which line correctly reads a whole number from the user?
q.why: Read the string, then convert it to an int.

q.q: Which method turns the text "1.75" into a decimal number?
q.why: Convert.ToDouble() converts to a double; ToInt32 is for whole numbers.

q.q: What does the 32 in Convert.ToInt32 mean?
o: It converts 32 characters at a time
It can only convert numbers up to 32
It converts to a 32-bit integer, which is what int is
q.why: int is a 32-bit integer.

q.q: What does the cast (int)4.99 give?
q.why: Casting to int chops off the decimal part; it does not round.

q.q: Converting an int to a double happens automatically. This is...
q.why: No data is lost, so it is implicit.

q.q: Why must a double to int conversion be explicit?
o: Doubles are always smaller than ints
C# does not allow conversion between number types
An int can hold any double without any loss
Data could be lost, because the decimal part is chopped off
q.why: You must ask for it with a cast such as (int).

q.q: The user types fourteen when the program uses Convert.ToInt32(). What happens?
o: The program stores 0 and carries on
The program asks the question again
The program crashes with a FormatException
q.why: Letters cannot be converted to an int, so a FormatException occurs.

q.q: Interactive programs follow which simple flow?
q.why: Programs gather data, react to it and give results.

q.q: What is 23 % 4?
q.why: 23 = 5 × 4 + 3, so the remainder is 3.

q.q: What does Console.WriteLine(11 / 4); print?
q.why: Both numbers are ints, so the remainder is thrown away: 11 / 4 = 2.

q.q: What does Console.WriteLine(7 / 2.0); print?
q.why: One number is a double, so the answer is a double.

q.q: What is 2 + 3 * 4 in C#?
q.why: C# follows BIDMAS: 3 × 4 = 12, then + 2 = 14.

q.q: In C#, what value does the expression (2 + 3) * 4 give?
q.why: The brackets are worked out first: 5 × 4 = 20.

q.q: A number n gives n % 2 equal to 0. What does that tell you?
q.why: A remainder of 0 when dividing by 2 means even; 1 means odd.

q.q: What does the % operator have to do with percentages?
o: It converts a decimal into a percentage
Nothing: it gives the remainder after division
It works out a percentage of a number
q.why: Modulus uses the percent sign but gives the remainder.

q.q: apple starts at 0. After apple = apple + 1; apple++; apple--; apple += 5; what is apple?
Which C# operator compares two values to see if they are the same?
q.why: Double equals compares; single = assigns.

q.q: In an IF ... ELSE statement, when is the code in the ELSE block run?
o: Only when there is an error
q.why: ELSE is the backup plan for a false condition.

q.q: Why is if (age = 18) not a correct way to check if someone is 18?
o: A single = assigns a value; C# uses == to compare
The number must be in double quotes
q.why: A single = assigns, and this won't even compile.

q.q: If mark is 50, what does if (mark < 50) {fail} else {pass} print?
q.why: 50 < 50 is false, so ELSE runs.

q.q: age = 14. Which condition is false?
q.why: 14 is not less than or equal to 13.

q.q: The user types left (all lower case) for if (choice == "Left"). What happens?
o: C# changes the input to Left automatically
The condition is true, because the letters are the same
The condition is false, because string comparisons are case-sensitive
The program crashes with a FormatException
q.why: "left" == "Left" is false.

q.q: With an IF ... ELSE IF ... ELSE chain, which block runs?
o: Only the first block whose condition is true
The last block whose condition is true
The ELSE block, then the first true block
Every block whose condition is true
q.why: C# checks each condition in order and runs only the first true one.

q.q: In AgeChecker, the user types 17. Conditions are age >= 18, then else if age >= 17, then else. What is printed?
o: You are old enough to drive, but not to vote yet.
You are old enough to drive and to vote.
You are too young to drive or to vote.
q.why: 17 >= 18 is false, then 17 >= 17 is true.

q.q: A program must print 'Number is not bigger than zero!' when the user enters 0 or less. Which condition is correct?
q.why: <= 0 includes 0 itself and all negatives; < 0 would miss 0.

q.q: Why do programmers use loops?
o: To write code once and run it as many times as needed
To make the computer choose which code to run
To store data in a named box in memory
q.why: Loops give iteration; DRY means Don't Repeat Yourself.

q.q: Which type of loop repeats a known number of times?
q.why: A count-controlled (for) loop runs a known number of times.

q.q: In for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++), what is the job of int i = 0?
q.why: e.g. int i = 0.

q.q: Which part of a for loop decides when the loop stops?
q.why: The loop stops when the condition is false.

q.q: How many times does the body of for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) run?
q.why: i takes the values 0 to 6, which is 7 passes.

q.q: What does for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) print?
q.why: When i reaches 5, i < 5 is false, so it stops at 4.

q.q: What does for (int i = 3; i <= 12; i += 3) print?
q.why: i goes 3, 6, 9, 12; 15 fails the condition.

q.q: In the running track loop, distance starts at 0 and 100 is added on each of 10 laps. What is the final distance?
A login program must keep asking until the correct password is typed. Which loop is best?
q.why: The number of attempts is unknown.

q.q: In while (myVar != "myPassword123"), what does != mean?
q.why: != is the C# version of ≠.

q.q: A WHILE loop checks its condition...
o: only at the end of the program
before each pass through the loop
q.why: It checks, runs, then checks again.

q.q: Why does an infinite loop never end?
o: The loop uses a for statement instead of while
The condition to stop the loop never becomes false
The loop variable is a string
q.why: So the loop never exits.

q.q: In the password program, what happens if myVar = Console.ReadLine(); is left out of the loop and the first password is wrong?
o: The program asks once more and then stops
The program accepts the wrong password
q.why: The variable is never updated, so the condition stays true.

q.q: How does Scratch's 'repeat until' differ from a C# while loop?
o: It always runs a fixed number of times, but while always runs forever
It keeps going until a condition becomes true; while goes while it is true
It checks the condition only at the end, but while never checks at all
There is no real difference: both stop as soon as the condition is true
q.why: They work in opposite ways.

q.q: Which is a sensible use of an infinite loop?
o: A traffic light system that must repeat forever
q.why: Traffic lights must cycle forever; the others should end.

q.q: A game lets the player keep guessing a secret number until they are right. Which loop is best and why?
o: For, because the counter starts at 1
For, because we know it will take 12 guesses
While, because it always runs exactly 10 times
While, because we don't know how many guesses it will take
q.why: The number of guesses is unknown.

q.q: In the guessing game, secretNumber is 42 and the user guesses 50, 25, then 42. What is attempts at the end?
q.why: attempts++ runs once for each of the three guesses.

q.q: What is a method?
o: A loop that repeats a known number of times
A text-only window where output appears
A storage box in memory that holds data
A named group of instructions that runs when it is called
q.why: Main, WriteLine and ReadLine are all methods.

q.q: What is a parameter?
o: A value passed into a method
q.why: It goes in the method's brackets.

q.q: Which keyword does AddTwoNumbers use to send its answer back to Main?
q.why: return gives back a value to where the method was called.

q.q: What does int answer = AddTwoNumbers(4, 7); store in answer?
q.why: The method adds num1 and num2 and returns 11.

q.q: In object-oriented C#, what is the template that objects are made from?
q.why: A class is the template; each object is an instance, like GameMaker objects and instances.

q.q: for and while loops belong to which of the core four building blocks?
q.why: Iteration means repetition.

q.q: Why should you add the loop last when building a program?
o: Loops must always be at the end of the code
To avoid infinite loops while testing
C# will not compile a loop added first
q.why: Get the inside working first, then wrap it in a loop.

q.q: What is the best way to test a partner's program?
o: Run it once with the input that they suggest to you
Try to break it with unexpected input, such as letters for a number
Check only that it compiles without any red errors
Count how many lines of code there are in the program
q.why: Unexpected input finds bugs.
